quarantines.reason: Saved youth and total unemployment outcomes both use the same ilostat:UNE_2EAP_SEX_AGE_RT_A file. The historical panel runner discarded sex and age dimensions and averaged every row by country/year before fitting only the first outcome, so the named youth series and registered youth-versus-total contrast were not measured.

The saved primary employment-to-population ratio came from ilostat:EMP_2EMP_SEX_AGE_NB, a count series with multiple sex and age rows per country/year. The historical panel runner averaged those counts without a population denominator; the recorded coefficient is not an employment-to-population rate.

The saved primary fit bridges ilostat:EMP_2EMP_SEX_AGE_RT_A to World Bank SL.EMP.TOTL.SP.ZS, a modelled total 15+ employment-to-population rate rather than the registered ILO ages-15–64 slice. The generic runner fits only that first outcome: the named long-term-unemployment secondary (loaded from an unfiltered general unemployment sex/age table without a duration measure), the within-five-years effect, and registered robustness checks were not tested. The public result card repeats the full claim and falsification rule while showing only one coefficient, so the saved verdict overstates its measured scope.
